FREEZING YOUR EGGS IN YOUR 30s

Fertility planning is becoming an important topic for many women, but decisions around egg freezing are often influenced by trends, online information, and individual circumstances.

Some important considerations include:

• Fertility potential may change with age
• Egg number and egg quality are both important factors in fertility discussions
• Conditions such as PCOS and Endometriosis can affect fertility experiences differently from person to person
• Previous ovarian procedures or medical history may be relevant in fertility planning
• Egg freezing is one option that may be considered as part of a broader fertility strategy

For some women, fertility preservation may be an option worth discussing. For others, timing and individual circumstances may differ.

Factors that may be considered include:

• age
• ovarian reserve assessment
• family planning goals
• relationship timelines
• medical history
• emotional and financial considerations

The focus should be on informed decision-making and understanding available options.

If you are considering fertility preservation, a discussion may include realistic expectations, fertility planning, and individualized guidance.

— Dr. Latika Chawla
Gynecological Endoscopic & Endometriosis Surgeon

Pelvic pain in Endometriosis can sometimes involve more than active disease alone.

For some women, ongoing discomfort may be influenced by multiple factors, including inflammation, tissue changes, muscle tension, movement patterns, and how the nervous system processes pain signals over time.

Adhesions are bands of scar tissue that may develop after inflammation, surgery, or disease processes. In some cases, they may affect how tissues and organs move in relation to one another.

Some women may experience symptoms such as:

• pelvic discomfort
• stiffness or restricted movement
• muscle tension
• increased sensitivity to pain
• reduced confidence with movement due to discomfort

Every experience can be different, and symptoms do not always correlate directly with the amount of visible disease.

This is one reason why endometriosis care often extends beyond treatment of disease alone and may also focus on overall function, movement, symptom management, and quality of life.

If pelvic symptoms continue after treatment or surgery, discussing them with your healthcare professional may help guide further evaluation.

Can having fewer periods extend fertility?

There has been recent discussion around fertility research and whether changes in menstrual patterns could one day influence reproductive aging.

Here’s the important context:

• Women are born with a finite ovarian reserve
• Fertility is influenced by several factors, including age, egg quality, hormones, genetics, and overall ovarian health
• Current evidence does not support reducing menstrual frequency as an established way to preserve fertility
• Research in this area is ongoing and is not part of routine fertility care today

An important question researchers continue to study is:

Can aspects of reproductive aging eventually be better understood or influenced in the future?

At present, there is no established treatment shown to extend fertility lifespan simply by reducing periods.

It is also important to remember that menstrual health, ovulation, hormone balance, and overall wellbeing are interconnected.

For women with:
• fertility concerns
• ovarian cysts
• endometriosis
• low AMH
• delayed family planning considerations

an individualized discussion and fertility assessment may help guide informed decisions.

Science continues to evolve, but healthcare decisions are best made using evidence-based information and personalized medical guidance.

Some exercises may feel different when living with Adenomyosis

Exercise is often encouraged for overall health and wellbeing, but every woman’s experience with Adenomyosis can be different.

Some women report that certain activities may be associated with symptoms such as:
• bloating
• pelvic heaviness
• cramps
• fatigue
• increased discomfort during flare phases

This does not mean exercise is harmful. Factors such as symptom patterns, pelvic floor tension, inflammation, and individual comfort levels may influence how the body responds.

During symptomatic phases, some women may find gentler activities more comfortable, such as:
• walking
• mobility exercises
• restorative yoga
• breathing practices
• guided pelvic health exercises

Movement is not one-size-fits-all, and what feels supportive can vary from person to person.

If pelvic symptoms are affecting your daily life or exercise routine, speaking with a healthcare professional may help guide the next steps.

— Dr. Latika Chawla
Consultant Gynecologist & Endometriosis Surgeon

Many women experience painful or heavy periods and assume it is a normal part of life.

Sometimes, these symptoms may be linked to conditions like adenomyosis, which can often go unrecognized in the early stages.

Symptoms such as increasing menstrual pain, heavy bleeding, pelvic discomfort, or a feeling of heaviness should not be ignored.

A timely gynecological evaluation can help identify the possible cause and guide women toward appropriate management options based on their individual health needs.

If your symptoms are affecting your daily life, consider consulting a qualified specialist for proper assessment.

PCOS is often misunderstood.

And now, many experts are reconsidering the name itself.

Why?

Because “Polycystic Ovarian Syndrome” does not fully explain what many women actually experience.

Many women with PCOS may not even have ovarian cysts. Instead, they struggle with:
• irregular periods
• acne and hair growth
• weight fluctuations
• insulin resistance
• fatigue
• fertility concerns

This is why the term PMOS (PolyMetabolic Ovarian Syndrome) is entering medical conversations.

The condition is not just about the ovaries. It is closely linked to metabolism, hormones, inflammation, and long-term health.

Early diagnosis and structured treatment can make a significant difference.

If you are experiencing persistent cycle irregularities or hormonal symptoms, do not ignore them.

— Dr. Latika Chawla
Consultant Gynecologist & Endometriosis Surgeon

Are GLP-1 medications like Ozempic affecting your periods or fertility?

GLP-1 medications (such as Ozempic and Mounjaro) are increasingly used for weight management and metabolic health. Some women may notice changes in their menstrual cycle or ovulation patterns after starting these treatments.

Here’s what is commonly observed:

• Improved insulin sensitivity may support more regular cycles in some women with PCOS
• Ovulation may resume, which can increase the chance of natural conception
• Absorption of oral contraceptive pills may vary, especially during dose adjustments
• These medications support metabolic health but are not a cure for PCOS
• They are not recommended during pregnancy and should be used under medical guidance

Every individual responds differently.

If you’ve noticed changes in your cycle after starting GLP-1 therapy, it’s important to discuss this with a qualified specialist.


— Dr. Latika Chawla
Gynecological Endoscopic & Endometriosis Surgeon

**Strategies to Improve Egg Quality and Number of Eggs**

Egg quality and egg number are crucial factors for successful conception, whether natural or through IVF. Egg number mainly depends on age and ovarian reserve, while egg quality reflects the genetic and metabolic health of the egg. Although new eggs cannot be created, the quality of existing eggs can be improved by optimizing the body’s internal environment.

A healthy lifestyle forms the foundation of good egg health. A balanced diet rich in proteins, antioxidants, fruits, vegetables, nuts, and healthy fats helps reduce oxidative stress on eggs. Maintaining an ideal body weight, avoiding smoking, alcohol, and excess caffeine, and ensuring adequate sleep are equally important. Stress reduction through yoga, meditation, or regular physical activity supports hormonal balance.

Medical optimization also plays a key role. Treating thyroid disorders, insulin resistance, and hormonal imbalances improves ovulation and ovarian response. Supplements such as CoQ10, myo-inositol, vitamin D, and omega-3 fatty acids may enhance egg quality when taken under medical supervision.

In IVF, individualized stimulation protocols, correct dosing, and precise timing can improve the number of mature eggs retrieved. Ultimately, improving egg quality and number is a gradual process, and early, personalized fertility care offers the best chance of success.
How to Improve Endometrial Thickness:

For pregnancy to occur, the uterus needs a healthy inner lining called the endometrium, where the embryo attaches and grows. In some women, this lining remains thin despite medicines, hormones, or fertility treatments. A thin endometrium can reduce the chances of embryo implantation, especially during IVF.

Mesenchymal Stem Cells (MSCs) are an advanced treatment option for women who do not respond to routine therapies. These special cells have the ability to repair and regenerate damaged tissues. They are usually obtained from safe sources such as the placenta or umbilical cord.

When MSCs are introduced into the uterus, they help improve blood flow, reduce scarring, and promote the growth of healthy endometrial tissue. Unlike treatments that work temporarily, MSC therapy aims to improve the overall quality of the uterine lining.

This therapy may benefit women with very thin endometrium, scarring after infections or surgery, or repeated IVF failures due to poor endometrial growth. MSC therapy is considered a specialized option and is recommended only after proper evaluation and counseling by a fertility specialist.

Your reproductive and women's health deserves expert attention at every stage of life. Whether you're dealing with irregular periods, PCOS, pregnancy care, menopause, or routine gynaecological check-ups, timely medical care can make all the difference.

Common reasons to visit a gynaecologist include:
• Irregular or painful periods
• PCOS and hormonal imbalance
• Pregnancy planning and antenatal care
• Menopause-related concerns
• Preventive women's health check-ups

Early consultation helps identify concerns before they become serious and supports better long-term health outcomes.

Trying to conceive but not seeing the results you hoped for? IUI (Intrauterine Insemination) may be a suitable fertility treatment for couples facing certain infertility challenges.

You may benefit from IUI if you have:
• Unexplained infertility
• Mild male factor infertility
• Ovulation-related issues
• Cervical factor infertility
• Difficulty conceiving naturally after trying for several months

IUI is a simple, minimally invasive fertility procedure that places specially prepared sperm directly into the uterus to improve the chances of pregnancy.

Every fertility journey is unique. Read our full blog to understand how IUI works, who it is suitable for, and what to expect during treatment.

Irregular periods, pelvic pain, unusual discharge, or persistent menstrual discomfort should never be ignored. These symptoms may indicate an underlying gynecological condition that requires timely medical attention.

A gynecologist can help with:
• Irregular or painful periods
• PCOS and hormonal imbalances
• Pregnancy and prenatal care
• Menopause management
• Routine women's health check-ups

Early diagnosis and the right treatment can help prevent complications and improve your overall reproductive health.

If you're experiencing any of these concerns, consult an experienced gynecologist for personalized care.

**Irregular Periods? It Could Be PCOD**

Irregular periods, unexplained weight gain, acne, or excessive hair growth may be signs of Polycystic Ovarian Disease (PCOD). Early diagnosis and the right treatment can help manage symptoms and improve your overall reproductive health.

Common signs of PCOD include:
• Irregular or missed periods
• Weight gain or difficulty losing weight
• Acne and oily skin
• Excess facial or body hair
• Difficulty conceiving

PCOD is a manageable condition with the right combination of medical care, lifestyle changes, and regular follow-up.

High-Risk Pregnancy? Expert Care Can Make All the Difference

A high-risk pregnancy requires specialized monitoring and timely medical support to help ensure the health of both mother and baby.

Some factors that may make a pregnancy high-risk include:
• High blood pressure during pregnancy
• Gestational diabetes
• Multiple pregnancy (twins or more)
• Maternal age above 35 years
• Previous pregnancy complications

My husband and I had been trying to conceive naturally for over two years without success. When we turned to Dr. Nikita for help with IVF, we immediately felt we were in the right hands.

Rather than letting the cycle go to waste, we tried IUI, but unfortunately, it didn’t work.

In February, I developed a cyst, and Dr. Nikita suggested a hysteroscopy to ensure everything was on track. Her thoroughness reassured us that she was doing everything possible to help us. By March, we started another round of injections, and this time, we retrieved four eggs. Out of those, only one was of good quality, but it developed into a grade-one embryo.

Dr. Nikita’s experience and instincts were incredible. She believed my uterus lining was perfect for implantation in the same cycle, and we trusted her advice. The result? A positive pregnancy and now a healthy baby girl!

Throughout this journey, Dr. Nikita’s calm approach, expertise, and support made all the difference. Even when the odds were against us and donor eggs were considered, she gave us hope and helped us achieve our dream.

We’re forever grateful to Dr. Nikita for making parenthood possible for us. If you’re struggling with fertility, I can’t recommend her enough—she truly works miracles!

featured_reviews.name: Jayant Kotian
featured_reviews.review_text:
I am writing to express my disappointment and frustration with the treatment and care provided by Dr. Swati for my wife's fibroid issue. We approached Dr. Swati in November 2024 and were suggested to undergo laparoscopic myomectomy. Despite initial hopes, the experience turned out to be quite disappointing.

## Issues with Treatment and Care
1. *Lack of desired outcome*: Despite undergoing surgery, my wife's condition did not improve significantly, and she had to undergo another surgery in January 2025 with a different doctor.
2. *Uncooperative behavior*: cashless in surya was not allowed as she wont get the desired payment and we were asked to get admitted in multispeciality hospital irla. This hospital was not up to the mark. Dr. Swati was not very cooperative over the phone for emergency queries post operation and we had to visit her multiple times for minor issues, which incurred additional costs. We were also made to pay for follow up visits and petty nurse injection charges

3. Long leave without proper care*: Dr. Swati went on a long leave for her daughter's wedding, leaving us with limited support and care during a critical period. Doctors should definitely go on long leave, but then should also avoid complex surgeries before going in such leaves. We were left with some assistant doctors number.

## Comparison with the Second Doctor
In contrast, the second doctor we consulted was fantastic. They were available for all our queries, charged less compared to Dr. Swati, and did not charge for follow-up visits. My wife is now fully recovered after the second surgery.

## Conclusion
Based on our experience, I would not recommend Dr. Swati for fibroid treatment. Her lack of availability, uncooperative behavior, and additional charges for procedures made the experience quite frustrating. We hope that Dr. Swati will take our feedback constructively and improve her services.

Rating: 1/5 stars
